record.title: OpenAI's V7 customer case describes a source-linked Context Graph for long-horizon agents
record.summary: In a September 21, 2026 customer story, OpenAI describes V7 Go's Context Graph as a persistent store of entities, relationships and source-linked facts extracted from enterprise files, queried directly with document search as a fallback. OpenAI reports that V7's retrieval-only system outperformed HERB's official baseline by 69% and reduced hallucinations on unanswerable queries by 38%; V7 also reports 78% lower cost per document with GPT-5.6 Luna than with GPT-5.4 mini, and 89% accuracy for GPT-6 Astra on its hardest graph-query set versus 78% for GPT-5.6 Sol. The HERB paper confirms the benchmark's enterprise-data setting and 39,190-artifact pool, but no V7 run configuration, absolute score, or independent reproduction was located. These are first-party customer-case results, not demonstrated general gains from knowledge graphs.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI describes V7 Go's Context Graph as extracting entities, relationships and facts from enterprise documents, preserving citations to source evidence, and serving graph queries with document search as a fallback when context is missing.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports that V7's retrieval-only system outperformed the official HERB baseline by 69% and reduced hallucinations on unanswerable queries by 38%; the V7-specific run configuration and absolute scores were not provided in the inspected account.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: V7 reports 78% lower cost per document with GPT-5.6 Luna than with GPT-5.4 mini, and 89% accuracy for GPT-6 Astra on its very-hard graph-query level versus 78% for GPT-5.6 Sol.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported results do not establish that graph memory generally improves agent accuracy, cost or workflow performance across vendors, datasets or customer deployments.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the V7 HERB retrieval results or the 38% unanswerable-query reduction was inspected.
The cost and graph-query comparisons omit the denominators and settings needed to compare cost per successful workflow or accuracy across models.
No customer-side evaluation measures whether the graph improves source citation fidelity, stale-fact handling, security permissions, or human review burden in deployed workflows.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported retrieval and workflow results survive matched testing, a persistent graph of source-linked enterprise facts with retrieval fallback could change how teams build long-horizon agents and evaluate context quality. The current account covers one vendor's system and supplies limited test details, so its consequence is meaningful but does not establish a general architecture advantage.
limitations: All V7-specific outcome numbers in the inspected OpenAI story are customer-case claims; no independent reproduction or customer-side audit was found.
The account gives no absolute V7 HERB score, test split/query count, retrieval configuration, comparison baseline version, uncertainty estimate or run logs.

The 78% cost comparison is per document against GPT-5.4 mini; the account does not state token, latency, quality target, batch, cache, or workflow conditions needed to generalize it to cost per successful task.
The GPT-6 Astra graph-query result uses V7's private test set; the article does not provide question count, difficulty calibration, scoring rubric or repeated-run variance.
HERB's published benchmark is synthetic enterprise data; results on it do not by themselves establish quality, privacy behavior or economic impact in real customer deployments.
The system description and product page are vendor-authored and do not compare source-linked graphs with alternative persistent-memory or retrieval architectures under a matched protocol.

technical.claimed_result: OpenAI reports that V7's retrieval-only system surpassed HERB's official baseline by 69% and reduced hallucinations on unanswerable queries by 38%. It also reports a 78% lower cost per document for GPT-5.6 Luna than GPT-5.4 mini, and 89% versus 78% accuracy for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 Sol on V7's very-hard graph-query set.
technical.demonstrated_result: The OpenAI customer story and V7 product page document the described Context Graph architecture and the reported measurements. The HERB paper establishes benchmark context, but the research desk did not reproduce the V7 runs or independently verify the results.
technical.mechanism: V7 Go ingests files from enterprise repositories, extracts entities, relationships, facts and attributes into a persistent Context Graph, links facts back to source documents, and exposes graph querying through MCP and repeatable workflows. OpenAI says V7 falls back to retrieval over underlying documents when the graph lacks enough information.
technical.regime: One vendor-reported enterprise product case involving finance, insurance and real-estate workflows. HERB is a synthetic enterprise benchmark with 39,190 artifacts and answerable/unanswerable queries. OpenAI's article does not provide V7's HERB system configuration, absolute scores, query counts, confidence intervals, hardware, or deployment cost accounting beyond the stated model comparison.
technical.strongest_baseline: For HERB, OpenAI says V7 compared its retrieval-only system to the benchmark's official baseline but does not identify the exact baseline implementation or V7 absolute results in the article. For per-document cost, GPT-5.4 mini is named as the comparison model. For the very-hard graph-query set, GPT-5.6 Sol is named as the comparison system. These are not a single matched evaluation across all reported outcomes.

brief.title: OpenAI's V7 customer case describes a source-linked Context Graph for long-horizon agents
brief.why_it_matters: Enterprise agents need context that persists across sessions and can be traced to documents, while large context windows and repeated search can make workflows costly and brittle. V7's Context Graph is a concrete product implementation of persistent, source-linked context with document retrieval as a fallback, and its customer story reports large retrieval and per-document cost gains. The reported numbers lack the setup and independent checks needed to show a general advantage, so the useful research question is whether this architecture lowers cost per correctly completed workflow while preserving provenance, permissions and correction handling.
